purpose: Documents full-text editorial review of newly downloaded posts before canonical ingestion.

posts.title: Committed Apologists and Serious Historians
posts.author: BDEhrman
posts.description: Argues that Christian apologists cease practicing serious history when theological commitments determine which miracle claims and Gospel accounts they accept.
posts.searchSummary: Argues that committed evangelical scholars can practice rigorous history only when theological commitments do not control their conclusions. Using Michael Licona's contrasting treatment of Jesus' resurrection and Matthew's raised saints, Ehrman shows how apologetic priorities can determine which miracle claims are accepted. He likewise challenges Licona's claim that intentional Gospel alterations preserve inerrancy and reliability, concluding that faith-based selection of historically trustworthy details is apologetics rather than critical history.

posts.title: Two Intrigues About Noah’s Flood
posts.author: BDEhrman
posts.description: Explains Genesis's three-storied cosmology and compares Noah's flood with Atrahasis and other ancient Near Eastern traditions, challenging modern literal readings.
posts.searchSummary: Explains two features of Noah's flood narrative: the three-storied universe assumed by Genesis and the story's relationship to older Near Eastern traditions. In biblical cosmology, the flood reverses creation as waters descend through the firmament and rise from beneath the earth. Comparing Noah with the Babylonian Atrahasis account, Ehrman argues that widespread flood myths more plausibly arose in flood-prone cultures and influenced one another than preserved a single worldwide catastrophe.

posts.title: Angels Seducing Women and the Rite of Circumcision: Two Peculiarities of Genesis
posts.author: BDEhrman
posts.description: Explains Genesis's stories of divine beings producing the Nephilim and circumcision marking Abraham's covenant, with parallels from neighboring cultures.
posts.searchSummary: Examines two unusual Genesis traditions: the sons of God mating with human women to produce the Nephilim, and circumcision as Abraham's covenant sign. Ehrman compares Genesis 6 with Greek myths in which gods father superhuman offspring, especially Zeus and Alcmene's son Heracles. He then traces circumcision as a wider ancient Near Eastern and possible puberty rite, using the Dinah and Shechem story to show its role in defining communal belonging.
topics: Divine Beings in the Hebrew Bible

posts.title: How Old Was Jesus When He Was Baptized?  And When He Died?
posts.author: BDEhrman
posts.description: Explains why Jesus is traditionally said to have died at thirty-three and why the Gospel evidence leaves his age highly uncertain.
posts.searchSummary: Examines the uncertain evidence for Jesus's age at baptism, the length of his ministry, and his age at death. Luke alone says Jesus was about thirty when baptized, while Mark suggests a ministry under a year and John's three Passovers imply more than two years. Ehrman contrasts the traditional age of thirty-three with Irenaeus's claim that Jesus approached fifty, concluding that no surviving source reliably establishes Jesus's age or ministry length.

posts.title: My Interview with James Carville
posts.author: BDEhrman
posts.description: Shares James Carville's wide-ranging, nonpolitical interview with Bart about Jesus, the Gospels, the Council of Nicaea, and related questions.
posts.searchSummary: Introduces James Carville's podcast and YouTube interview with Ehrman, arranged unexpectedly and conducted without political discussion. Ehrman describes Carville as a prominent political strategist and says the informal conversation ranges from Jesus and the Gospels to the Council of Nicaea. The post does not summarize Ehrman's answers or develop those subjects itself; it shares the recording with permission and presents the exchange as an enjoyable, wide-ranging interview.
